title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page states a proposition. Let C be a category and A a full subcategory. Let 𝒞 and 𝒞' be sets of index categories. Assume C is stable under inductive limits of type 𝒞 and projective limits of type 𝒞'. Assume every object of C is both a 𝒞-colimit and a 𝒞'-limit (in C) of objects of A. Then C is equivalent to two things: (i) the full subcategory Â_𝒞 ⊂ Â = Hom(A°, Ens) of presheaves that are 𝒞-colimits of representables; (ii) the opposite of the full subcategory (A°)^_𝒞' ⊂ Hom(A, Ens) of copresheaves that are 𝒞'-colimits of corepresentables. In the additive case one uses Â_ab and Hom(A, Ab) instead.

This page makes the statement precise as an essentially commutative diagram. On the left, A ⊂ C is sent by id on A and by an equivalence r : C → Â_𝒞 into A ⊂ Â_𝒞 ⊂ Â. This is the restricted Yoneda embedding X ↦ Hom(-,X)|_A. On the right, by id on A and an equivalence r' : C → ((A°)^_𝒞')° ⊂ ((A°)^)°. This is the restricted co-Yoneda embedding X ↦ Hom(X,-)|_A.

Composing gives a 'remarkable equivalence' Â_𝒞 ≃ ((A°)^_𝒞')°. It is a duality between a category of presheaves on A and a category of copresheaves on A, both built from A alone.

Grothendieck then poses the problem: define intrinsically, in terms of A, 𝒞 and 𝒞' only, a category D. It should sit in Â (or as an additive subcategory of Â_ab), be stable in Â under 𝒞-colimits, and admit 𝒞'-limits. He stresses these limits are 'not necessarily the same as in Â!'. Every object of D should be at once a 𝒞-colimit of objects of A and a 𝒞'-limit of such functors. In effect, D is the universal C for which the proposition applies.

Worked example: A has a single object, in the additive case, so A is a ring R. Take 𝒞 = 𝒞' = finite discrete categories, i.e. finite (bi)products. Then Â_𝒞 is the category of finitely generated free right R-modules, and (A°)^_𝒞' is finitely generated free left R-modules. The equivalence becomes the classical anti-equivalence M ↦ Hom_R(M, R) between f.g. free right and left modules. This is continued on the next page ('dualité de tels modules'). The next page goes on to a universal property: Hom_{𝒞'-cont}(C, C') → Hom(A, C') is fully faithful, marked 'à vérifier'. In the additive case Hom_add(C, C') ≃ Hom_{½add}(A, C').

Purpose within the manuscript (dévissage of ∂-perfect complexes): an abstract framework for categories of 'perfect' objects generated by a small A. It explains the self-duality of such categories (free/projective modules, perfect complexes) as an instance of a limit/colimit duality.
errors: As stated, the proposition (previous page) needs more hypotheses. Being a 𝒞-colimit of A-objects does not by itself make the restricted Yoneda functor C → Â fully faithful (A need not be dense). Nor does it send 𝒞-colimits in C to 𝒞-colimits in Â. So the identification of C with the presheaves that are 𝒞-colimits of representables, colimits computed in Â, can fail. It works when the relevant colimits are absolute (e.g. finite biproducts in the additive case, as in the example) or when A is dense and the colimits are preserved. Grothendieck partly flags this: 'pas nécessairement les mêmes que dans Â!' here, and 'à vérifier' on the next page.
The problem statement mixes 'stable in Â under 𝒞-colimits' with each object being a colimit 'dans C'. Presumably 'dans D' is meant; minor.

ideas.what: C ≃ Â_𝒞 ≃ ((A°)^_𝒞')° when every object of C is both a 𝒞-colimit and a 𝒞'-limit of objects of a full subcategory A, giving a duality between presheaf-type and copresheaf-type completions of A
ideas.modern_name: Isbell conjugation / Isbell duality; objects fixed by the Isbell adjunction (reflexive completion, Isbell envelope); dense and codense subcategories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Isbell (1960, 1966); Kelly, Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory (1982), ch. 5; Avery–Leinster, 'Isbell conjugacy and the reflexive completion' (2021)
ideas.where_published: Ind-objects and pro-objects appear in SGA 4 Exp. I and in Pursuing Stacks; this specific two-sided equivalence is not known to me in published Grothendieck texts

ideas.what: Problem: intrinsically characterise (from A, 𝒞, 𝒞') the category generated by A under 𝒞-colimits whose objects are also 𝒞'-limits of A-objects, with 𝒞'-limits possibly differing from those in Â
ideas.modern_name: Free completion under a class of colimits preserving (or creating) a class of limits; limit-colimit sketches; free bicompletion / MacNeille-type completion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ehresmann (sketches), Gabriel–Ulmer (1971), Kelly (1982), Albert–Kelly (1988), Joyal (free bicompletion, 1995)

ideas.what: Example: A = one-object additive category (a ring R), finite discrete index categories, giving the anti-equivalence f.g. free right R-modules ≃ (f.g. free left R-modules)^op via Hom(-, R)
ideas.modern_name: Duality of finitely generated free/projective modules; additive (Cauchy) completion of a ring
ideas.where_published: Standard; used in SGA 6 for perfect complexes

missed.claim: Grothendieck views the classical duality of f.g. free (perfect) modules as a special case of an abstract equivalence Â_𝒞 ≃ ((A°)^_𝒞')°. This is essentially Isbell duality restricted to a class of colimits and limits, i.e. a relative reflexive completion. He wants it as a tool for dévissage of perfect complexes. Framing the duality of perfect objects as a 'restricted Isbell duality' was only made systematic much later (Avery–Leinster reflexive completion; work on Cauchy completeness and duality).
missed.quote: On trouve en particulier une équivalence remarquable Â_𝒞 ≃ (Â°_𝒞')°
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests treating dualities of perfect or compact objects (Perf ≃ Perf^op) via relative Isbell conjugation with prescribed classes of limits and colimits. This is a mild conceptual link, not a new theorem.

missed.claim: He poses the problem of intrinsically defining the 'universal' category D generated by A under 𝒞-colimits whose objects are simultaneously 𝒞'-limits, with limits possibly different from those in Â. On the next page the needed universal property is left 'à vérifier'.
missed.quote: Il s'agit de définir intrinsèquement en termes de A, 𝒞, 𝒞' ... (pas nécessairement les mêmes que dans Â!)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is largely answered in later work on completions under mixed classes of limits and colimits. Historically it shows Grothendieck thinking about such completions in 1975–76.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is essentially Isbell duality and dense/codense completion, known since the 1960s–80s, plus a classical module duality. It is interesting only as evidence of Grothendieck's framework for dévissage of perfect complexes; the general proposition needs hypotheses he only partly flags.
transcription_corrections: Diagram: the arrows from C are 'id' to A and 'r' (marked ≃) to Â_𝒞 on the left. On the right they are 'id' to A and 'r'' (marked ≃) to ((A°)^_𝒞')°. r and r' are the restricted Yoneda and co-Yoneda equivalences.
'(resp. sous Â_ab et Â°_ab)' — in the additive case, subcategories of Â_ab and (A°)^_ab.
'Si A est réduite : un seul objet' is better read as 'Si A est réduite à un seul objet' (A a ring), in the additive case.

Final lines likely read: 'on trouve une anti-équivalence entre modules libres de type fini à gauche et à droite' (continued on the next page), rather than 'une équivalence ... modules libres de type fini'.
'dans C d'objets de A' and 'dans C de tels foncteurs' in the problem statement probably refer to D (the category being defined).
